narrative:
The model estimated an 82% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied. This is a high-risk score, meaning your profile looked much closer to borrowers who had repayment problems than to those who repaid well.

The strongest reason was your checking account status: it shows a negative balance (below zero DM). Among approved applicants, only about 12.6% had this status, while 59.2% had no overdraft. This was the largest factor pushing your application toward bad credit. The second strongest factor was the requested loan duration of 48 months, far longer than the approved average of about 19 months; a longer commitment increases the time and uncertainty over repayment. Third, your savings of under 100 DM added risk because it leaves little financial cushion if income or expenses change. Savings below 100 DM are common among approved applicants, but in your case this weaker buffer reinforced the other concerns rather than offsetting them.

To improve your chances next time, focus on reducing or clearing the overdraft, shortening the requested loan term or lowering the amount, and building a more stable savings buffer before reapplying. You could also ask the bank what monthly payment it considers affordable and whether adding a reliable co-applicant or guarantor would strengthen a future application.
